questions.question_text: Which of the following statements does not reduce cognitive dissonance in a cocaine user?

options.text: I have more chances of dying when crossing a road than injecting cocaine
Smoking is worse killer than cocaine use
Alcohol affects the whole body while cocaine is not that bad
Even Freud used cocaine in those days, there must be something good about it

questions.explanation: 'I like cocaine very much' is likely to increase not decrease the dissonance.

questions.question_text: At what age do children pass the mirror test?
questions.explanation: Mirror test-A test for self-recognition in which the child using its mirror image to touch a dot on its nose is achieved at 18 months of age.

questions.question_text: Which of the following increases the effectiveness of a persuasive communication?
questions.explanation: The credibility of a perceived message is a crucial factor in persuasion.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes a self-serving bias?

options.text: A person attributes other people's behaviour to internal sources
A person attributes other people's behaviour to external sources
A person attributes successes to external sources
A person attributes successes to internal sources
A person attributes failures to internal sources

correct_answer.text: A person attributes successes to internal sources

correct_answers.text: A person attributes successes to internal sources

questions.explanation: Self-serving bias-people show a strong bias towards attributing their success to internal causes while attributing failures to situational causes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors reduce cognitive dissonance?

options.text: Adding one or more alternative cognitions

correct_answer.text: Adding one or more alternative cognitions

correct_answers.text: Adding one or more alternative cognitions

questions.explanation: Dissonance is lowered if the behaviour is altered; cognitions are dismissed, and new cognitions are added.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true concerning primate psychology?

options.text: Aggressive male baboons have longer life expectancy
Aggression is higher during periods of instability
Young baboons learn appropriate expression of aggression by observing their peers
Low ranking baboons are not aggressive
Among baboons, females are not aggressive

correct_answer.text: Aggression is higher during periods of instability

correct_answers.text: Aggression is higher during periods of instability

questions.explanation: During periods of instability such as rank transition, baboons show higher levels of aggression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to influence individuals to conform to the views of the group?

options.text: Individuals feel accepted by the group

questions.explanation: Ambiguous tasks tend to lead to more conformity as people may feel less certain of their own ideas.

questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly describes fundamental attribution error?

options.text: Refusing to accept one's own errors
Denying the fundamental flaws behind one's own negative behaviour
Attributing others mistakes to the context in which the mistakes occur
Attributing one's own mistakes to one's character and personality
Attributing others mistakes to their personal dispositions

correct_answer.text: Attributing others mistakes to their personal dispositions

correct_answers.text: Attributing others mistakes to their personal dispositions

questions.explanation: Fundamental Attribution Error refers to overestimating dispositional factors and not situational factors while attributing causes to other’s behaviours.

questions.question_text: The theory of mind is not well developed in which of the following disorders?
questions.explanation: Theory of mind: An understanding that other people possess mental states that involve ideas and views of the world that are different from our own.

questions.question_text: The first aspect of self-concept to develop is the
questions.explanation: Bodily self-refers to the ability to differentiate one's own body from that of others.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct with regard to cognitive dissonance? It is a:

options.text: Method of choice for solving abstract problems

questions.explanation: The principle of cognitive consistency is the focus of Festinger's (1957) theory of cognitive dissonance.

questions.question_text: The individual behaviour of group members is less important than that of the whole group. What is this concept called?
questions.explanation: Deindividuation is a process where people lose their sense of socialized individual identity and resort to unsocialized and antisocial behaviours.

questions.question_text: Individuals often tend not to intervene when someone seeks help, especially when others who can offer help are present in the vicinity. In social psychology, this phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility: people feel that the responsibility is not theirs, and someone else will do something.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a behavioural component of Allport's concept of prejudice?
questions.explanation: Prejudice is essentially an attitude. Hence, it has cognitive component – stereotypes; affective component – hostility; and behavioural component – discrimination.

questions.question_text: In a small group situation, under which of the following conditions departures from norms are most likely to be tolerated?

options.text: The norms were stated frequently during previous meetings
Dissent comes from a member with strong credentials
A consensus was reached before the dissent was expressed

correct_answer.text: Dissent comes from a member with strong credentials

correct_answers.text: Dissent comes from a member with strong credentials

questions.explanation: Norm rejection is more easily achieved in the absence of enforcement and more readily tolerated if the rejecting member possesses strengths and abilities needed by the group.

questions.question_text: Aggression is a consequence of frustration. Who proposed this hypothesis?
questions.explanation: According to Berkowitz, aggressive-cue hypothesis frustration provokes anger, not aggression.

questions.question_text: A patient feels unhappy with respect to one aspect of his life. Soon he observes that this unhappiness affects several other aspects of his life as well, resulting in a depressed state of mind. Which of the following types of cognitive bias is most likely to be relevant to this description?
questions.explanation: Domino effect is the psychological equivalent of the butterfly effect in chaos theory.

questions.question_text: The attributional bias seen in persecutory delusions are
questions.explanation: It has been proposed that individuals with persecutory delusions make excessive external attributions of the cause for negative events.

questions.question_text: The term 'cognitive dissonance' was coined by
questions.explanation: Festinger coined the term 'cognitive dissonance'.

questions.question_text: The Likert scale consists of
questions.explanation: The Likert scale consists of five responses to each statement- Agree/disagree on a five-point scale.

questions.question_text: In a social psychology experiment, audience attended a convention where speakers were randomly allocated to speak in favour of or against an important political issue. The audience were told beforehand that the attitudes of the speakers were determined by a coin toss. Despite this, the subjects rated speakers who spoke in favour of the subject as having on average a more positive attitude towards the issue than those who spoke against it. Which of the following does this indicate?
questions.explanation: We tend to explain behaviour in terms of internal disposition, such as personality traits, abilities, motives, etc.

questions.question_text: Several people at a train station see an elderly man asking for help. None of the onlookers offer to help. This is explained by
questions.explanation: This is called bystander apathy or Genovese effect.

questions.question_text: A depressed patient has shown a good degree of improvement in her sleep pattern after initiating a new treatment. Though objectively she continues to be depressed, when using a self-rated scale to monitor her symptoms, she significantly overrates the degree of improvement in her mood and other domains. This effect is called
questions.explanation: The halo effect refers to a cognitive bias whereby the perception of a particular trait is influenced by the perception of other related traits.

questions.question_text: If a person's performance of a task is influenced by test procedures used, this is called
questions.explanation: The Hawthorne effect refers to the tendency of some people to work harder and perform better when they are a part of an experiment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following accurately reflects instrumental aggression?

options.text: It is carried out using destructive weapons
It is motivated by negative feelings

questions.explanation: Instrumental aggression is carried out for the purpose of achieving a particular goal, e.g., kidnapping for ransom.

questions.question_text: Task completion is poor in which of the following types of leadership?
questions.explanation: Task completion is good in autocratic and democratic leaderships but poor in groups led by a leader with laissez-faire style.

questions.question_text: Vulnerability to conform with the group is more in those that are
questions.explanation: Less intelligent members conform more than those with higher IQ.

questions.question_text: The vulnerability to conform is greater in individuals with which of the following characteristic features?
questions.explanation: People who are naive are more likely to conform, especially to members of their own group.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered to be a factor of social influence when a group makes a polarized decision?
questions.explanation: Normative influence: People have a need not to appear odd or 'stick out' as a sore thumb.

questions.question_text: The classic studies by Milgram explain the concept of
questions.explanation: The classic studies by Milgram show that people would obey orders under certain conditions even if these exceeded the bounds of their usual beliefs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can reduce groupthink?
questions.explanation: Various strategies that can reduce groupthink include encouraging open debate and acknowledging the presence of groupthink.

questions.question_text: A team leader is constantly calling for her group to focus on its commitment to the overall outcomes more than anything else. She is following a
questions.explanation: Persuasion is the ability to motivate and enthuse the group to pursue the goal.

questions.question_text: In a dark room, several lights are turned on and off in rapid succession. An observer perceives a single light as moving from one position to the next rather than different lights coming on and off at different positions. What is this called?
questions.explanation: The phi phenomenon is an optical illusion based on the principle that the human eye is capable of perceiving movement from pieces of information.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a secondary drive?
questions.explanation: Competence or secondary drives are those, which people seek out, but which do not fulfil a physiological need like play.

questions.question_text: The semantic differential scale may be subject to which of the following problems?
questions.explanation: The semantic differential scale is a visual analogue scale that may be subject to various biases.

questions.question_text: A candidate who has appeared for a mock exam before the actual exam does well than a candidate who has not. This is called
questions.explanation: Practice effects occur when a participant performs the same task twice and can improve performance in the second instance.

questions.question_text: What factor is the most influential in the development of friendly relationships?
questions.explanation: A classic study identified proximity as a major factor affecting the probability of making an acquaintance.

questions.question_text: In Milgram's obedience experiments, the factors that increased obedience include all except

options.text: Relieving the subject from responsibility of actions

questions.explanation: Being proximal to shocked victim will reduce shock administering behaviour and so reduce obedience.

questions.question_text: The most common effect of cognitive dissonance is
questions.explanation: Cognitive dissonance is an aversive psychological state aroused when there is a discrepancy between actions and attitudes.

questions.question_text: The power in a person due to his ability to provide positive accomplishments is known as
questions.explanation: Reward power is the power that is conveyed through rewarding individuals for compliance with one's wishes.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is defined by how much we approve of ourselves and how worthy we think of ourselves?
questions.explanation: Self-esteem refers to how much we approve of ourselves and how worthy we think of ourselves.

questions.question_text: Tom is a student who attributes a good grade on an exam to his intelligence and hard work but a poor grade to the teacher's poor ability and unfair test questions. He is exhibiting;
questions.explanation: A self-serving attributional bias refers to individuals attributing their successes to internal or personal factors but attributing their failures to external or situational factors.

questions.question_text: The presence of others reduces task performance. This is called
questions.explanation: Social loafing is a phenomenon where individuals exert less effort when working as part of a group.

questions.question_text: Attitudes do not always correlate with one's behaviours. The attitudes that most accurately predict behaviour are those that are

options.text: Not based on one's own life experiences

questions.explanation: Attitudes predict behaviour if they are strong and consistent and based on direct experience.

questions.question_text: Scapegoating refers to

options.text: Tension between racial groups rise when the economic conditions are similar
Encouraging conflicts with a political motive
Sexual assault on a vulnerable group leading to conflicts
Lack of empathy on perpetrators of abuse
Captives becoming emotionally attached to the captivators

correct_answer.text: Tension between racial groups rise when the economic conditions are similar

correct_answers.text: Tension between racial groups rise when the economic conditions are similar

questions.explanation: Scapegoats are singled out victims who are blamed and discriminated by virtue of their group membership.

questions.question_text: A mother of an autistic child is curious to know the reason behind her son's apparent lack of empathy towards other children of similar age. Which of the following concept is relevant to address her question?
questions.explanation: Lack of Theory of Mind (ToM) may be the explanation for the apparent lack of empathy among children with autism.

questions.question_text: According to the frustration-aggression hypothesis which of the following is false?

options.text: Aggression is the one of the many possible responses to frustration
Fear of punishment can inhibit aggression
Aggression is driven by a need to nullify frustration
Unavailability of the frustrator can inhibit aggression
Unexpressed frustration cannot be displaced onto an innocent target

correct_answer.text: Unexpressed frustration cannot be displaced onto an innocent target

correct_answers.text: Unexpressed frustration cannot be displaced onto an innocent target

questions.explanation: In a meta-analysis, evidence showed that frustrated individuals show displacement of aggression from the source of frustration onto a less powerful or more accessible target.
